questions.questionText: hour Additional Materials: Multiple Choice Answer Sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) READ THESE INSTRUCTIONS FIRST Write in soft pencil. Do not use staples, paper clips, highlighters, glue or correction fluid. Write your name, Centre number and candidate number on the Answer Sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. There are forty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any working should be done in this booklet. questions.questionText: The density of the material of a coil of thin wire is to be found. Which set of instruments could be used to do this most accurately?

options.C: stopwatch, newton-meter, vernier calipers
options.D: tape measure, vernier calipers, lever balance Space for working

questions.questionText: A quantity X varies with temperature θ as shown. X 0 100°C θ θ is determined from the corresponding values of X by using this graph. X is measured with a percentage uncertainty of ±1% of its value at all temperatures. Which statement about the uncertainty in θ is correct?

options.A: The percentage uncertainty in θ is least near 0°C.
options.B: The percentage uncertainty in θ is least near 100°C.
options.C: The actual uncertainty in θ is least near 0°C.
options.D: The actual uncertainty in θ is least near 100°C.

questions.questionText: The measurement of a physical quantity may be subject to random errors and to systematic errors. Which statement is correct?

options.A: Random errors can be reduced by taking the average of several measurements.
options.B: Random errors are always caused by the person taking the measurement.
options.C: A systematic error cannot be reduced by adjusting the apparatus.
options.D: A systematic error results in a different reading each time the measurement is taken. Space for working

questions.questionText: The velocity of an electric car changes as shown. velocity /kmh–1 0 1 2 3 4 time/s What is the acceleration of the car?
A ball is thrown vertically in air. Neglecting air resistance, which property of the ball can never be zero at any time during the flight?

options.C: speed

questions.questionText: A golf ball is hit with the same force and direction on the Earth and on the Moon. Which diagram best represents the shapes of the paths taken by the golf ball?

options.C: D Moon Moon Earth Earth Space for working

questions.questionText: An object travelling with velocity v strikes a wall and rebounds as shown. v v Which property of the object is not conserved?

options.C: momentum

questions.questionText: A particle X has speed v and collides with a stationary identical particle Y. The collision is perfectly elastic. X Y v What are the speed and direction of motion of each of the two particles after the collision? X Y

options.A: stationary v to the right v v
options.B: 2 to the right 2 to the right v v
options.C: 2 to the left 2 to the right
options.D: v to the left stationary Space for working

questions.questionText: A mass of 2.0kg rests on a frictionless surface. It is attached to a 1.0kg mass by a light, thin string which passes over a frictionless pulley. The 1.0kg mass is released and it accelerates downwards. mass pulley 2.0kg 1.0kg 0.50m What is the speed of the 2.0kg mass as the 1.0kg mass hits the floor, having fallen a distance of 0.50m?

options.A: 1.8ms–1 B 2.2ms–1 C 3.1ms–1 D 9.8ms–1 Space for working

questions.questionText: A lead pellet is shot vertically upwards into a clay block that is stationary at the moment of impact but is able to rise freely after impact. stationary clay block mass 95g impact velocity 200ms–1 lead pellet mass 5.0 g The pellet hits the block with an initial velocity of 200ms–1. It embeds itself in the block and does not emerge. How high above its initial position will the block rise? (Mass of pellet = 5.0g; mass of clay block = 95g.)

options.A: 5.1m B 5.6m C 10m D 2000m Space for working

questions.questionText: The diagram shows an experiment to measure the force exerted on a ball by a horizontal air flow. 30° air flow The ball is suspended by a light string and weighs 0.15N. The deflection of the string from vertical is 30°. What is the force on the ball from the air flow?

A student balances a 30cm ruler on a fulcrum set at the 15cm mark. She then places a 50g mass on the 23cm mark and a 20g mass on the 11cm mark, as shown. 20g 50g 0 7 11 23 30 Which mass should she place on the 7cm mark to restore the balance?

options.A: 30g B 40g C 47g D 133g Space for working

questions.questionText: A sledge slides down a slope at a constant velocity. The three forces that act on the sledge are the normal contact force C, the weight W and a constant frictional force F. Which diagram represents these forces acting on the sledge?

options.C: C F F

questions.questionText: The kinetic energy of a particle is increased by a factor of 4. By what factor does its speed increase?

A piston in a gas supply pump has an area of 600cm2 and it moves a distance of 40cm during one stroke. The pump moves the gas against a fixed pressure of 5000Pa. How much work is done by the piston during one stroke?

options.A: 1.2 × 102J B 1.2 × 104J C 1.2 × 106J D 1.2 × 108J Space for working

questions.questionText: A railway engine accelerates a train of total mass 800 tonnes (1 tonne = 1000kg) from rest to a speed of 50ms–1. How much work must be done on the train to reach this speed?

Water from a reservoir is fed to the turbine of a hydroelectric system at a rate of 500kgs–1. The reservoir is 300m above the level of the turbine. The electrical output from the generator driven by the turbine is 200A at a potential difference of 6000V. What is the efficiency of the system?
Which row correctly describes the spacing, ordering and motion of the molecules in water and in ice when both are at a temperature of 0°C? spacing ordering motion

options.A: molecules in ice are a regular pattern of molecules in both ice closer together than molecules in both ice and water have the molecules in water and water same average speed
options.B: molecules in ice are a regular pattern of molecules in ice travel closer together than molecules in ice but not more slowly than those molecules in water in water in water
options.C: molecules in ice are a regular pattern of molecules in ice travel further apart than molecules in both ice more slowly than those molecules in water and water in water
options.D: molecules in ice are a regular pattern of molecules in both ice further apart than molecules in ice but not and water have the molecules in water in water same average speed Space for working

questions.questionText: Three springs are arranged vertically as shown. P Q R W Springs P and Q are identical and have spring constant k. Spring R has spring constant 3k. What is the increase in the overall length of the arrangement when a force W is applied as shown? 5W 4W 7

The diagram shows the stress-strain graph for two wires X and Y of different materials up to their breaking points. Both wires have the same initial dimensions. X stress Y strain Which statement is not correct?

options.B: Material X extends more than material Y when loaded with the same force.
options.C: Material X has a larger ultimate tensile stress.

options.A: 2 B 4 C 8 D 16 Space for working

options.C: D displacement displacement 0 0 0 0 time time Space for working

questions.questionText: What do not travel at the speed of light in a vacuum?

options.C: radio waves

Monochromatic light is directed at a diffraction grating as shown. Which diagram shows all the possible directions of the light, after passing through the grating, that give maximum intensity?

options.A: B C D Space for working

options.C: D velocity velocity 0 0 0 time 0 time Space for working

The separation of the plates is doubled. What will be the new force on the particle? F F

options.A: 0.040A B 0.11A C 9.0A D 25A Space for working

questions.questionText: A cylindrical wire of length 10m and diameter 2.0mm has a resistance of 0.050Ω. From which material is the wire made? material resistivity/Ωm

options.C: silver 1.6 × 10–8

questions.questionText: The I-V characteristics of two electrical components P and Q are shown below. 2.0 I/A 1.5 P Q 1.0 0.5 0 2.0 4.0 6.0 8.0 V/V Which statement is correct?

options.A: P is a resistor and Q is a filament lamp.
options.B: The resistance of Q increases as the current in it increases.
options.C: For a current of 1.9A, the resistance of Q is approximately half that of P.
options.D: For a current of 0.5A, the power dissipated in Q is double that in P. Space for working

questions.questionText: In a fire alarm system, a thermistor T has a resistance of 2000Ω at room temperature. Its resistance decreases as the temperature increases. The alarm is triggered when the potential difference between X and Y reaches 4.5V. 12V T 150Ω X Y What is the resistance of the thermistor when the alarm is triggered?

A network of electrical components is connected across a battery of negligible internal resistance, as shown. V A The resistance of the variable resistor is increased. What is the effect on the readings of the ammeter and voltmeter? ammeter voltmeter

options.C: unchanged decreases

A class of students used dice to simulate radioactive decay. After each throw, those dice showing a ‘6’ were removed. The graph shows the results. number of dice remaining 0 2 4 6 8 10 number of throws of the dice What could the scatter of points about the best-fit curve represent for actual radioactive decay?

options.A: background count not being taken into account
options.B: more than one type of radiation being present
options.C: the random nature of radioactive decay
options.D: the spontaneous nature of radioactive decay Space for working

questions.questionText: Which statement about alpha, beta and gamma radiation is correct?

options.A: Alpha radiation has the greatest ionising power.
options.B: Beta radiation has the greatest ionising power.
options.C: Gamma radiation has the greatest ionising power.
options.D: Alpha, beta and gamma radiation have nearly equal ionising powers.

questions.questionText: In a radioactive decay series, three successive decays each result in a particle being emitted. The first decay results in the emission of a β-particle. The second decay results in the emission of an α-particle. The third decay results in the emission of another β-particle. β α β P Q R S Nuclides P and S are compared. Which statement is correct?

options.A: P and S are identical in all respects.
options.B: P and S are isotopes of the same element.
options.C: S is a different element of lower atomic number.
options.D: S is a different element of reduced mass.
